claim: Automatic tensor program auto-scheduling (DietCode) can reduce compilation time on dynamic-shape workloads
conditions: Language modeling workload; compared to existing tensor program auto-scheduler baseline
quote: DietCode reduce the compilation time by up to 5.88× on the state-of-the-art language modeling workload compared with the existing tensor program auto-scheduler
paper: Automatic Compiler-based Optimizations for Deep Neural Networks

claim: Compiler-based optimizations can incur measurable runtime overhead as a tradeoff cost
conditions: GPU memory footprint optimization (Echo); training state-of-the-art DNNs
effect: 1% runtime performance overhead from recomputation optimization
quote: we can significantly reduce the GPU memory footprint by up to 3.13× with only 1% runtime performance overhead
paper: Automatic Compiler-based Optimizations for Deep Neural Networks

claim: Graph breaks force execution to fall back to Python eager mode, introducing costly CPU-GPU synchronization
conditions: PyTorch 2 with TorchDynamo/TorchInductor; code patterns that cause graph breaks
effect: Costly CPU-GPU synchronization and reduced optimization opportunities leading to slower execution
evidence: Core finding from GraphMend investigation; identified as primary problem affecting compiled model performance
quote: certain code patterns still cause graph breaks that force execution to fall back to Python eager mode, introducing costly CPU-GPU synchronization and reducing optimization opportunities
paper: GraphMend: Code Transformations for Fixing Graph Breaks in PyTorch 2

claim: Cold-start compilation overhead differs dramatically from steady-state performance
conditions: PyTorch 2 torch.compile on NVIDIA GPUs; GraphMend-fixed models on 27 models with graph breaks
effect: Up to 26x cold-start speedup and 5x average, but only 1.39x steady-state forward pass speedup
evidence: Experimental measurements in GraphMend evaluation; direct comparison of cold vs. steady-state phases
quote: GraphMend achieves up to 26x cold-start speedup, 5x on average, and up to 1.39x steady-state forward pass speedup
paper: GraphMend: Code Transformations for Fixing Graph Breaks in PyTorch 2

claim: Graph breaks are prevalent in real model deployments despite PyTorch 2 improvements
conditions: Analysis of 195 HuggingFace transformer models; PyTorch 2 era
effect: 13.8% of production models contain unfixed graph breaks that silently degrade performance
evidence: Systematic investigation of HuggingFace model collection
quote: Our investigation of 195 Hugging Face models reveals that 13.8% of models exhibit graph breaks
paper: GraphMend: Code Transformations for Fixing Graph Breaks in PyTorch 2

claim: Eliminating graph breaks enables larger uninterrupted FX graphs and better optimization
conditions: Semantics-aware source-level transformations applied to graphs with breaks; PyTorch 2 compilation pipeline
effect: Improved performance through increased graph size and optimization opportunities without developer refactoring
evidence: GraphMend eliminated 107 of 147 graph breaks (73%), fully fixing all breaks in 21 models with measurable speedup
quote: These transformations enable PyTorch to capture larger, uninterrupted FX graphs without manual refactoring by developers
paper: GraphMend: Code Transformations for Fixing Graph Breaks in PyTorch 2
